title: D3Q27 activation in GeneralSimEngine — predeclared verification protocol

decision.question: Is LatticeModel.D3Q27 in tensorlbm.general_sim.GeneralSimEngine a REAL, verified capability (equilibrium/streaming/bounce-back/far-field/force/mass-correction on the 27-direction stencil), and does it measurably improve sphere drag accuracy over the shipped D3Q19 path at the same grid?
alternatives: A0 (status quo): D3Q27 stays a dead enum; GeneralSimEngine remains D3Q19-only (gaps.md G7/G8).
A1 (implemented): add lbm_step_d3q27 (far-field 27 + verified main loop) and wire collide/init/mass/force dispatch; keep D3Q19 path bit-identical.
A2 (rejected): run the D3Q27 stencil through the D3Q19 kernels (wrong stencil, silent corruption) — rejected by construction.
decision.decision_rule: A1 accepted iff gates (a)(b)(c)(d)(e)(f)(g)(h)(i) of the campaign node all pass on the recorded artifacts; any failing gate is reported as honest FAIL and not overridden.

hypotheses.H1: The D3Q27 lattice is not an accuracy advantage on a staircase sphere at D=20 for Re=100 drag (both lattices are 2nd order; the staircase force-integration error dominates).
hypotheses.H2: Both lattices converge at >=1.8 order in space on a smooth Taylor-Green field with an exact analytic reference, D3Q27 not worse than D3Q19.
hypotheses.H3: The activated D3Q27 path conserves mass to <1e-12 (relative) in a closed periodic domain and does not drift the drag plateau.

metrics.a_equilibrium_isotropy: max rank-3 moment residual of d3q27.equilibrium27 at rest and rank-4/6 lattice-tensor identities (float64)
metrics.b_mass_conservation: |M(t)-M(0)|/M(0) after 200 periodic D3Q27 steps with a solid sphere (float64)
metrics.c_sphere_Re100_cd_error: |Cd_plateau - Cd_SchillerNaumann(100)| / Cd_ref * 100 (D=20, MRT, quadratic wall-pressure extrapolation)
metrics.e_d3q27_vs_d3q19_cd_error_ratio: Cd error of D3Q19 divided by Cd error of D3Q27 at identical grid/settings
metrics.f_tgv_l2_order: observed log2(E(24)/E(48)) of the L2 velocity error vs the exact z-invariant Taylor-Green solution (grids 24/48/96, float64)
metrics.g_d3q19_degenerate_residual: max |macroscopic27(embed(f19)) - macroscopic3d(f19)| and streaming/BB residuals on the D3Q19 subspace
metrics.h_mrt_stability_re200: finite field after 10 000 MRT steps at Re=200 with a plateau drift < 2%

sphere.geometry: parametric sphere, radius 0.5 m, D = 20 lattice cells
sphere.domain: engine auto domain (70x60x60 lattice units, blockage 2.4%)
sphere.plateau_window: mean over the last 25% of steps; drift checked against the 50-75% window
sphere.force_integration_primary: pressure_extrap='quadratic', p0_method='near_wall' (documented best integration; 'none' is the known G12 systematic-bias path and is run for Re=100 as a secondary diagnostic)
sphere.reference: Schiller-Naumann 24/Re(1+0.15 Re^0.687) = 1.0917 (Re=100), 0.8064 (Re=200); Clift-Gauvin stored as cross-reference

tgv.case: Taylor-Green on the periodic torus; z-invariant field (exact solution of the 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes: u_x = A e^{-2 nu k^2 t} sin(kx) cos(ky), u_y = -A e^{-2 nu k^2 t} cos(kx) sin(ky), u_z = 0, k = 2 pi / N)
tgv.metric: E(N) = ||u_N(T) - u_exact(T)||_2 / ||u_exact(T)||_2 on the grid's own nodes; order = log2(E24/E48) and log2(E48/E96)

environment.solver: TensorLBM worktree branch agent/m6648 (tensorlbm.lbm_step_d3q27 + general_sim D3Q27 dispatch)
environment.compute: cluster nodes n315/n330 (loong64, 128 cores each, torch 2.13.0), CPU-only (no GPU on the nodes), torch.set_num_threads 32-48
environment.dtype: float32 for the sphere runs (production), float64 for the analytic gates

analysis.aggregation: plain arithmetic mean over the declared plateau windows; no outlier removal
analysis.uncertainty: plateau drift between adjacent windows and the tail-window spread are reported; no uncertainty claim beyond them
analysis.stopping_rule: fixed step counts; runs stop early only via the divergence guard (non-finite state), which is recorded

deviations.statement: The first TGV attempt used convective scaling (U0 = 0.05 fixed, tau -> 1/2 under refinement). It gave observed order 0.84 (runs/tgv_convergence_convective_scaling.json) — the O(h) acoustic-scaling regime rather than the 2nd-order diffusive regime. The gate is therefore measured with diffusive-style fixed tau and an exact analytic reference.

A full-3D (z-dependent) Taylor-Green self-convergence study was run first (diffusive scaling, Re=20, grids 24/48/96) and did NOT converge: E(24)=2.5e-3, E(48)=2.8e-3, order -0.18; the D3Q19 control reproduced the same plateau (order -0.02), so the plateau is a property of that self-convergence protocol (grid-independent acoustic/initial-layer content), not of the D3Q27 wiring. It is reported as an honest limitation of the protocol; gate (f) is measured on the exact-reference z-invariant TG instead, which has no nonlinearity/compressibility floor.
A pilot of 20 steps (D=12) was run only to verify the engine wiring and one 3-step timing probe to size the cluster jobs; no Cd value was inspected before these thresholds were fixed.

safety_resource_limits.memory: D3Q27 fields at 252k cells = 27 MB per copy (float32); the step holds at most 3 copies
safety_resource_limits.cluster: job timeout 2400-3600 s per node, 32-48 threads per shard, two nodes
